memos.headline: MSFT and NVDA Lead Near Highs; UNH in Freefall, AAPL and GOOGL Lagging SPY
memos.body: I see a clear two-tier market within our universe today. MSFT and NVDA are the standout leaders—both within 4% of their 52-week highs, well above their 50d and 200d means, with 12-week relative strength vs SPY of +17.5% and +15.9% respectively. JPM is similarly strong at just -1.8% from its high with solid relative strength, though RSI at 68 and XOM at 71 suggest short-term overbought conditions that warrant caution on fresh entries. On the other side, UNH is in a catastrophic downtrend: -51.7% from its 52-week high, 19% below its 50d mean, 40% below its 200d mean, and RSI at 36.6—this is a falling knife with no sign of stabilization. AAPL and GOOGL are both underperforming SPY meaningfully over 12 weeks and trading below their 200d means, making them unattractive until trend structure improves.

views.note: Trading within 0.6% of 52w high, +13.4% above 200d mean, RSI 69 not yet extreme, and dominant +17.5% relative strength over 12w—I'd reconsider below the 50d mean (~435).
Near highs at -3.7% drawdown, +14.6% above 50d mean with +15.9% 12w relative strength; RSI 62.5 has room, but I'd cut if it breaks below ~125 (200d mean area).
Just -1.8% from 52w high with +13.3% above 200d mean and positive relative strength across all timeframes; RSI 68 is elevated so I'd size modestly and reassess below 255.
Down 51.7% from 52w high, 19% below 50d mean, 40% below 200d mean with RSI 36.6 and -44.4% 12w relative strength—this is a broken chart and I see no reason to step in front of it.
Trading 10.2% below its 200d mean with -13.4% 12w relative strength vs SPY and -22.4% drawdown from highs; would need a reclaim above the 200d mean (~224) to reconsider.
RSI 44.6, -19.3% from highs, below 200d mean by 3%, and -5.6% 12w relative strength—trend is weak and I'd need a close above ~172 (200d area) to turn neutral.
Strong 4w move of +10.7% but RSI 71.4 is overbought and 12w relative strength is still -4.9%; I'd wait for a pullback toward the 50d mean (~106) before getting involved.
Sitting +8.7% above 50d mean but barely above 200d mean and still -13.5% from highs; trend is improving but not yet confirmed—watch for a break above 380 for conviction.
Middling setup: +6% above 50d mean but only +2.8% above 200d mean with -1.3% 12w relative strength; needs to clear ~220 to show real momentum.
Below both 50d and 200d means with RSI 39.8 and -5.8% 4w relative strength; defensive name acting defenseless—would reconsider above 165 (50d area).

memos.headline: GOOGL and MSFT Show Durable Earnings Power; CAT and XOM Flash Cash-Flow Compression Warnings
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe between names with accelerating earnings and those facing margin headwinds. GOOGL posted 46% YoY net income growth on 12% revenue growth with a 38.3% net margin and only $14.79B in total debt—the best margin-leverage combination in the group. MSFT delivered 17.7% net income growth on 13.3% revenue growth at a 36.9% net margin, confirming durable operating leverage in its cloud mix shift. On the other side, CAT's revenue fell 9.8% YoY with net income collapsing 29.8%, compressing margins to 14.1%, which signals cyclical deterioration I'm unwilling to pay through. XOM's flat revenue and -6.2% net income decline at a thin 9.3% margin leave little room for error if commodity prices soften further. I would need to see CAT's revenue stabilize and XOM's margins expand before reconsidering either name.

views.note: 46% YoY net income growth, 38.3% net margin, and minimal leverage at $14.79B debt make this the cleanest earnings compounder in the group.
13.3% revenue growth translating to 17.7% net income growth at a 36.9% margin demonstrates durable operating leverage from the cloud mix shift.
69.2% YoY revenue growth and a 42.6% net margin are extraordinary, but net income growth of 26.2% lagging revenue growth signals rising costs that I need to monitor.
64.2% YoY net income growth on 8.6% revenue growth shows massive margin expansion to 11.0%, though $58.75B in debt and heavy capex could compress free cash flow.
Revenue +5.1% and net income +4.8% are steady but unexciting; $92.20B in total debt is the highest in the tech group and limits upside conviction.
Solid 32.3% net margin and 9.1% net income growth, but the bank's $407B debt stack and macro sensitivity keep me at neutral.
Revenue declined 2.1% YoY with net income barely positive at +0.4%; the 19.1% margin is stable but top-line shrinkage is a concern.
Revenue grew 9.8% but net margin is only 5.7% with $81.27B in debt and no comparable YoY net income figure available, limiting my visibility.
Revenue down 9.8% and net income down 29.8% YoY with margin compressing to 14.1%—classic cyclical deterioration I refuse to pay for.
Flat revenue and a 6.2% net income decline at a 9.3% margin leave no cushion; I'd need to see margin expansion before reconsidering.

memos.headline: Fed on Extended Pause at 4.50% With Softening Labor Market — Favor Duration-Sensitive Growth, Neutral Banks
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in pause mode: the upper bound has held at 4.50% for three months while the effective rate sits at 4.33%, unchanged over the same window. CPI is running at just 2.4% year-over-year, which is close enough to target that the next move is more likely a cut than a hike, but the Fed clearly isn't in a hurry. The unemployment rate has crept up to 4.3%, rising 40bp over the past year, signaling a gradual labor-market softening that tilts the regime toward late-cycle slowdown rather than outright recession. The 10y-2y spread has normalized sharply to +0.44pp (up 91bp y/y), and the 10y yield at 4.38% has drifted higher over three months, suggesting the long end is pricing in fiscal supply and sticky nominal growth rather than imminent easing. A July CPI print above 0.3% m/m or unemployment jumping to 4.5%+ would change my regime call — the former delays cuts further, the latter accelerates them.

views.note: Duration-sensitive mega-cap growth benefits from a pause-to-easing trajectory with 2.4% CPI keeping real rates from rising further.
Similar duration tailwind as MSFT; benign inflation and a stable-to-lower rate path support premium multiples on long-duration cash flows.
Growth-oriented name gains from pause regime, though elevated 10y yield at 4.38% caps how far multiples can expand near-term.
Positive 10y-2y spread of 44bp supports NIM, but rising unemployment (+40bp y/y) raises credit-loss provisions — offsets roughly balance.
Cyclical bellwether faces headwinds from softening labor market and no imminent easing; not yet bearish but upside is capped.
Staples offer defensive positioning in a slowdown, but 2.4% CPI limits pricing power upside and 4.38% 10y yield compresses the dividend premium.
Late-cycle slowdown with rising unemployment typically pressures energy demand; macro setup is unfavorable for cyclical commodities.
Consumer-facing growth name benefits from moderating inflation (2.4% y/y) preserving real spending power and a Fed poised to ease eventually.
Ad-driven revenue resilient in mild slowdown; duration tailwind from pause-to-cut regime supports valuation.
Defensive healthcare name is macro-insensitive; no strong macro signal either way at current rate and inflation levels.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Divergence: MSFT and NVDA Positive Momentum vs. AAPL Drag and UNH Leadership Churn
memos.body: I am reading the post-earnings price reactions and 8-K filing cadence across the universe as of June 20. MSFT's +7.6% earnings-day pop on Apr 30 was the strongest signal in the group, suggesting a genuine narrative upgrade that likely attracted further positive coverage. NVDA followed with a solid +3.2% reaction on May 28, reinforcing the AI-capex theme. AAPL stands out negatively with a -3.7% post-earnings drop and a follow-on 8-K on May 12, suggesting unresolved concerns that may still weigh on tone. UNH has filed four separate Departure/Appointment 8-Ks between late April and early June—an unusually high cadence of leadership turnover that I expect is generating persistently negative or uncertain media sentiment, and I do not think the market has fully discounted the governance noise.

views.note: The +7.6% earnings reaction is the strongest in the universe and likely catalyzed a sustained positive tone shift that still has room to run.
A +3.2% post-earnings move on May 28 confirms constructive sentiment around AI demand; tone should remain supportive near-term.
The -3.7% earnings-day decline signals a negative tone shift, and the subsequent May 12 filing suggests lingering issues that may keep sentiment soft.
Four officer departure/appointment 8-Ks in six weeks is an abnormal cadence of leadership churn likely generating persistent negative media tone.
Near-flat -0.1% earnings reaction and only routine proxy filings since suggest no strong directional tone signal.
Muted +0.6% earnings reaction and subsequent routine filings leave sentiment roughly balanced with no clear catalyst.
No earnings price reaction data available; the Deutsche Bank presentation and officer announcement suggest active investor engagement but no clear tone direction.
A trivial +0.4% earnings reaction and routine proxy filing point to flat sentiment with no narrative shift.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty Falling Fast but VIX Spike and Oil Surge Signal Residual Geopolitical Risk
memos.body: I note that the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index has dropped 44% over three months to 315.71, suggesting the worst of the tariff/sanctions shock narrative is fading, yet VIX has jumped 22% in the past month to 22.17, and WTI crude has surged nearly 19% over the same period to $75.89/bbl—pointing to an energy-security or supply-disruption catalyst that has not fully resolved. High-yield spreads remain well-behaved at 3.16%, down slightly on both 1m and 3m horizons, so credit markets are not pricing a hard landing from policy tightening. The 10y-2y spread at +0.44pp, up 19bp over three months, is consistent with a normalizing curve rather than imminent recession. My conviction is highest where I can trace a clear geopolitical transmission channel—AAPL's China/tariff supply-chain exposure, NVDA's export-control overhang, XOM's energy-security tailwind, and CAT's infrastructure/trade-policy sensitivity—and lower where the link is indirect. A re-escalation of US-China export controls or a new round of tariffs would be the key policy action that would change my views.

views.note: Export-control overhang on advanced AI chips to China remains a structural headwind; any tightening of October 2022/2023 rules would be a clear negative catalyst.
China assembly concentration and tariff risk persist despite the recent drop in policy uncertainty; the May 8-K filing adds opacity but no clarity on supply-chain shifts.
WTI up ~19% in a month to $75.89 reflects tightening supply or geopolitical risk premium, directly benefiting XOM's upstream margins; energy-security policy tailwinds remain intact.
Three 8-K filings in six weeks suggest active investor communication amid trade-policy flux; infrastructure spending is supportive but tariff uncertainty on imported steel/components caps conviction.

Defensive staples benefit from falling policy uncertainty and stable credit spreads; multiple recent Reg FD disclosures suggest proactive guidance, and geopolitical risk is a second-order concern here.
Steepening yield curve (+19bp over 3m) is modestly positive for NIM, but elevated VIX and residual geopolitical uncertainty keep me from a high-conviction call.
